title: Calculations and measurements of torque and inductance of switched reluctance motors with laminated and composite magnetic cores

source.citation: M. Przybylski, Archives of Electrical Engineering 71(1), 2022, pp. 125-138

related.citation: M. Przybylski, Modelling and analysis of the low-power 3-phase switched reluctance motor, Archives of Electrical Engineering 68(2), 2019, pp. 443-454
related.use: The original (parallel-wound) motor's analysis and dimensions. Not downloaded: the user did not approve it, so nothing is taken from it.

machine.topology: inner rotor 12/8 switched reluctance motor (a modified Emerson Electric H55BMBJL-1820 washer motor): tapered salient stator poles with free-standing coil blocks, parallel-sided salient rotor poles
machine.symmetry: Full cross-section with A = 0 on the stator's outer circle, as the authors' model in Fig. 1(a). Phase A alone is excited: its four coils (poles at 0, 90, 180 and 270 degrees) in series with alternating polarity. The rotor turns by remeshing.

components_map.part: stator: twelve tapered salient poles, slot bottoms on an arc
rotor: eight parallel-sided salient poles, slot bottoms on an arc
24 quadrilateral coil blocks drawn free in the slots
three phases of four series coils, 172 turns each, polarities as Fig. 1(a)
air in the slots and the gap

rotor_outer_diameter_mm.note: Fig. 1(a) puts two rotor-face nodes at 41.49 mm: the rotor's diameter, so the stator faces lie at 41.9 mm.

air_gap_mm.note: Fig. 1(a): stator-face nodes at 41.95 mm (8 nodes, spread 0.11 mm), 0.46 mm outside the rotor.

core_length_mm.quote: Axial length of magnetic core 47.3 46.6 mm

turns_per_coil.note: Turns of each pole's coil; a phase is four coils in series (gap 'winding'): Table 2's current linkage is 172 times the phase current.

stator_pole_arc_table_deg.note: Recorded; the model uses Fig. 1(a)'s 15.0 degrees (stator_pole_arc_deg). Control table-pole-arcs builds 15.5.

rotor_pole_arc_table_deg.note: Recorded; the model uses Fig. 1(a)'s parallel 10.96 mm poles (15.2 degrees). Control table-pole-arcs builds 16.

phase_resistance_ohm.note: Not used by a static solve. Checks the series winding: 688 turns of 0.56 mm copper with a 0.14-0.15 m mean turn give 6.7-7.2 ohm at 20 C (8.2-8.8 ohm near 75 C); 172 turns in all would give under 2 ohm.

inductance_current_A.quote: Emerson Electric motor were executed at the amplitude of currents equal to … = 0.7 A
inductance_current_A.note: The paper's inductance simulations: flux linkage over current at this amplitude, with the amplitude (AC) curve.

steel_bh.figure: Fig. 6, p. 131: magnetization curves of the electrical steel, 1 - AC 50 Hz (black), 2 - DC (grey)
steel_bh.scale_reference: Gridlines at 0-4000 A/m and 0-1.6 T, least squares over all of them: misfit 4.2 A/m and 0.001 T; 8.38 A/m and 0.0042 T per pixel
steel_bh.note: Fig. 6 curve 2 (DC), which the paper used for torque: H at fixed B, local quadratic fits to the curve's pixel track (largest spread between fit windows 8.9 A/m). Uncertainty about 10 A/m (one pixel) below 1.2 T; above it the AC and DC curves coincide within a pixel or two and one track serves both, within 0.01 T. The reading's permeability at 300 A/m is 1508 against the quoted 1600 (control steel-quoted-permeability). FEMM extends the curve beyond 1.58 T itself; the paper's plots show at most 1.4 T in the motor.

steel_bh_ac.figure: Fig. 6, p. 131: magnetization curves of the electrical steel, 1 - AC 50 Hz (black), 2 - DC (grey)
steel_bh_ac.scale_reference: Gridlines at 0-4000 A/m and 0-1.6 T, least squares over all of them: misfit 4.2 A/m and 0.001 T; 8.38 A/m and 0.0042 T per pixel
steel_bh_ac.note: Fig. 6 curve 1 (AC 50 Hz, amplitudes), which the paper used for its inductance simulations; the variant ac-curve builds the steel with it. Largest fit spread 8.9 A/m; permeability at 300 A/m 937 against the quoted 1000. Recorded here for its provenance; the variant carries the same values.

stacking_factor.reason: The paper names no lamination fill and measured the curves on toroidal samples cut from the motor's own sheet; FEMM's default fill of 1 applies the measured curve to the whole core, as the authors' FEMM model most likely did.

shaft_material.reason: Fig. 1(a) fills the shaft with the cores' grey; the paper names no shaft material. Taken as the core steel; control shaft-air makes it non-magnetic. The rotor core carries 0.25-0.7 T (Section 3.2), so the shaft carries little flux.

gaps.item: dimensions beyond Table 1 (pole roots, yoke, rotor roots, shaft, pole taper, coil outline)
gaps.note: The 2019 companion paper is unavailable (not approved for download). Fig. 1(a) is a rendering of the authors' FEMM model with its node markers; scaled by the 139.5 mm stator and checked by the 83 mm rotor, the markers locate nodes within about 0.08 mm.

gaps.item: pole arcs: Table 1 states 15.5 and 16 degrees; Fig. 1(a) shows 15.0 and 15.2
gaps.affects: torque plateau and the inductance's slope
gaps.note: The model is built as Fig. 1(a) shows, since the targets are that model's results (as in hamouda-2019-srm-8-6); control table-pole-arcs builds Table 1's angles.

gaps.affects: every target, most at low current where the steel's initial permeability matters
gaps.note: Fig. 6 digitized (DC for torque, AC amplitude for inductance, as Section 2 and 3.3 state). The readings' permeability at 300 A/m is 6% below the quoted 1600 and 1000; control steel-quoted-permeability scales H by 0.94.
The core steel, as Fig. 1(a)'s grey suggests; control shaft-air.

gaps.affects: every flux linkage, inductance and torque
gaps.note: Four 172-turn coils in series per phase: the text says the coils were changed from parallel to serial, Table 2's current linkage is 172 times the phase current, and the 8.4 ohm resistance needs about 688 turns of the 0.56 mm wire.
0 degrees aligned, 22.5 unaligned: Fig. 9's inductance is largest at 0 and Fig. 11's torque falls to zero at both ends.

gaps.item: which build the inductance targets come from
gaps.note: The AC amplitude curve at a 0.7 A amplitude (Section 3.3); the variant ac-curve is that build. Torque uses the DC curve (Section 2).
About 100,000 elements (Section 3.2); the model's own mesh plus control mesh-0p6.

gaps.item: the prototype SMC motor (Table 1 and 2's second column, Fig. 1(b))
gaps.note: A different machine: round-bottomed rotor slots and stator outlines no component draws, two further Somaloy curves (Fig. 4, 5). Left for a separate case.
Measured inductances and torques are comparators, as the paper's own 2D FEMM differs from them by 5-40%.

variants.purpose: The paper's inductance simulations: the same machine with the steel's AC 50 Hz amplitude curve (Fig. 6 curve 1, the parameter steel_bh_ac) instead of the DC curve its torque simulations used. Carries the inductance targets; its torques are diagnostics.

controls.purpose: Every explicit mesh size and arc segment at 0.6 times (about the paper's 100,000 elements).
Table 1's pole angles: 15.5 degree stator faces (the taper kept, the roots widened as much as the faces) and 16 degree parallel-sided rotor poles.
The DC curve with H times 0.94, so its permeability at 300 A/m matches the quoted 1600 (a one-pixel shift of the reading).

coverage.reproduced: The modified Emerson Electric motor: Table 2's FEMM maximum and average static torque at 0.6, 1 and 1.6 A, and the FEMM aligned and unaligned inductance at 0.7 A (Section 3.3 with Table 1); Table 1 and 2's measurements, Fig. 9(a)'s inductance curve, Fig. 10(a)'s flux linkage and Fig. 11's torque curves as comparators.
coverage.not_reproduced: The SMC prototype (Fig. 1(b), Table 1-2 second columns), the magnetization measurements themselves, the flux density maps of Figs. 7-8, Fig. 13, and Table 2's eq. (1) column (an analytic formula over Fig. 10, reported as a diagnostic).
